from money import format_pln, split_cents


def receipt_lines(total: int, people: list) -> list:
    """One line per person with their share of the bill."""
    shares = split_cents(total, len(people))
    shares[-1] += total % len(people)
    return [f"{name}: {format_pln(share)}" for name, share in zip(people, shares)]
import unittest

from receipt import receipt_lines


class ReceiptLinesTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_even_bill(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            receipt_lines(3000, ["Ala", "Ola", "Ela"]),
            ["Ala: 10,00 zł", "Ola: 10,00 zł", "Ela: 10,00 zł"],
        )

    def test_every_grosz_is_paid(self):
        self.assertEqual(
            receipt_lines(1000, ["Ala", "Ola", "Ela"]),
            ["Ala: 3,33 zł", "Ola: 3,33 zł", "Ela: 3,34 zł"],
        )

Fixed. `split_cents(100, 3)` now returns `[33, 33, 34]`. The leftover grosze go one each to the last people in the list, so the shares always add up to the total.

**I also changed `receipt.py`.** `receipt_lines` was working around the bug by adding `total % len(people)` to the last person's share. With the fix in place, that line would have charged the leftover grosze twice, so I removed it. One side effect: when two grosze are left over, they now go to two different people instead of both landing on the last one (1001 split three ways gives 333/334/334, not 333/333/335).

Because I touched `receipt.py`, I ran `test_receipt.py` along with `test_money.py`, and all 6 tests pass. I didn't run the full suite. I also added a test to `test_money.py` that checks uneven splits and confirms the shares always sum to the total.

Fixed. `split_cents(100, 3)` now returns `[33, 33, 34]`. The leftover grosze go one each to the last people in the list, so the shares always add up to the total.

**I also changed `receipt.py`.** `receipt_lines` was working around the bug by adding `total % len(people)` to the last person's share. With the fix in place, that line would have charged the leftover grosze twice, so I removed it. One side effect: when two grosze are left over, they now go to two different people instead of both landing on the last one (1001 split three ways gives 333/334/334, not 333/333/335).

Because I touched `receipt.py`, I ran `test_receipt.py` along with `test_money.py`, and all 6 tests pass. I didn't run the full suite. I also added a test to `test_money.py` that checks uneven splits and confirms the shares always sum to the total.
